terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, deponent: the person in the dative, the threat in the accusative or ablative
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1.102: crucem minārī alicui (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The person threatened is in the dative (mihi minātur), the threat in the accusative or the ablative. “Threaten to do” is accusative and infinitive: minātus sēsē abīre (Plaut. As. 3.3.14). Properly, of rocks, to jut out (Verg. A. 1.162).
The frequentative of minor, common in comedy and in Cicero, with the same constructions.

phrases.english: to threaten someone, have it in for someone

sources: Lewis & Short: minor · Lewis & Short: minitor
